glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The pre-election voter registration deadline for Idaho's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 23, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. local time. Eligible voters who miss the deadline may still register when voting in person during early voting or on Election Day.

Election Day Registration: Idaho allows qualified voters to register and vote at their designated polling place on Election Day. In-person registration requires an accepted photo ID and proof of residence.

No-Excuse Absentee Voting: Any registered Idaho voter may request an absentee ballot. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, absentee-ballot applications must be received by the county clerk by 5:00 p.m. local time on October 23.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Idaho residents can register online, submit a voter registration form to their county clerk, register in person at the county clerk's office, or register when voting in person during early voting or on Election Day. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old, and have been a resident of Idaho and the county for at least 30 days before the election. A person convicted of a felony may not register until the terms of the sentence have been completed. Online registration requires a current Idaho driver's license or Idaho identification card.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, county office or same-day registration
register.internal_note: The official registration page directly establishes registration methods, citizenship, age, 30-day Idaho residence requirement, felony eligibility rule and online identification requirement. Idaho permits registration when voting in person during early voting and on Election Day. In-person registration requires current photo identification and proof of residence.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Idaho's official Voter Information Lookup to check your voter registration record. The VoteIdaho.gov voter tools also provide information about your assigned Election Day polling location and personalized ballot information.
check_registration.internal_note: VoteIdaho.gov provides the official Voter Information Lookup and links it directly from the 2026 General Election page. The General Election page directs voters to the lookup to check registration and polling information.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Idaho's pre-election voter registration deadline is October 23, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. local time. Eligible voters who miss that deadline may register when voting in person during early voting or at their designated polling place on Election Day. In-person registration requires accepted photo identification and proof of residence.
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar directly establishes October 23 at 5:00 p.m. local time as the preregistration deadline. The official registration page, [https://voteidaho.gov/voter-registration/](https://voteidaho.gov/voter-registration/), confirms registration during early voting and on Election Day and lists the required identification and proof-of-residence documents.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Idaho voters voting in person on Election Day must go to the voting location assigned to their physical residential address. Use VoteIdaho.gov's official voting-location tool or Voter Information Lookup to find your assigned polling place. Early-voting locations are determined by each county and may be different from Election Day polling locations.
polling_place.glance_value: Vote at your assigned Election Day location
polling_place.internal_note: The official FAQ directly states that Election Day voters must visit their assigned voting location based on physical address. The 2026 General Election page, [https://voteidaho.gov/idaho-general-election/](https://voteidaho.gov/idaho-general-election/), provides both the polling-location finder and Voter Information Lookup.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Idaho polling places are open from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Voters must use their designated Election Day polling place. Qualified individuals may register and vote at their designated polling place on Election Day by providing the identification and proof of residence required for registration. Registered voters are required to present an accepted photo ID when voting in person.
election_day.internal_note: The official Election Day calendar entry directly establishes November 3, 2026, 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. polling hours and Election Day registration at the designated polling place, citing Idaho Code §§ 34-211, 34-408A and 34-1101. Identification requirements are independently confirmed by [https://voteidaho.gov/frequently-asked-questions/](https://voteidaho.gov/frequently-asked-questions/) and [https://voteidaho.gov/voter-registration/](https://voteidaho.gov/voter-registration/).

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Idaho polling places are open from 8:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, polling places and county clerks' offices are scheduled to be open during those hours.
polling_hours.internal_note: The official 2026 Election Day calendar entry directly establishes 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. hours and cites Idaho Code §§ 34-211, 34-408A and 34-1101.

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Idaho counties may provide in-person early voting before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting may begin October 13 and must end by 5:00 p.m. on October 30 in counties that conduct early voting. Locations, starting dates and daily hours are determined locally, so voters should check with their county elections office for the schedule that applies to them.
early_voting.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar states that early voting may begin October 13 for the November 3 election in counties choosing to conduct early voting and that in-person absentee/early voting ends at 5:00 p.m. October 30. The 2026 General Election page currently summarizes the voter-facing early-voting period as October 13-30 but directs voters to county details. Because counties determine whether, where and when to conduct early voting within the statutory period, exact local schedules should not be inferred.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Idaho voter may request an absentee ballot; no excuse is required. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the county clerk must receive the absentee-ballot application by 5:00 p.m. local time on October 23. Completed absentee ballots must be received by the county clerk by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day, November 3. A late postmark does not substitute for timely receipt. Idaho also has certain designated mail-ballot precincts, which are separate from ordinary voter-requested absentee voting.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Request by October 23; ballot due November 3
absentee_mail.internal_note: VoteIdaho.gov states that any registered voter may request an absentee ballot. The official 2026 calendar at [https://voteidaho.gov/calendar/category/voter-registration-absentee-requests/](https://voteidaho.gov/calendar/category/voter-registration-absentee-requests/) establishes the October 23 application deadline at 5:00 p.m. The election calendar at [https://voteidaho.gov/calendar/list/?tribe-bar-date=2026-10-01](https://voteidaho.gov/calendar/list/?tribe-bar-date=2026-10-01) establishes the November 3, 8:00 p.m. receipt deadline. The calendar separately identifies designated mail-ballot precincts, so statewide absentee-by-request should not be confused with county-designated mail precincts.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Idaho requires registered voters voting in person to present an accepted photo ID. Accepted identification includes an Idaho driver's license or Idaho identification card, a U.S. passport or federal photo identification card, a tribal identification card, or a concealed weapons license issued by an Idaho county sheriff. Idaho's current voter guidance no longer lists a signed personal identification affidavit as an alternative to presenting photo identification. Voters registering in person must also provide proof of residence.
voter_id.internal_note: The current official FAQ directly lists the accepted photo-ID categories for already registered voters. The official registration page, [https://voteidaho.gov/voter-registration/](https://voteidaho.gov/voter-registration/), lists the same photo IDs for registration and separately requires proof of residence. Idaho changed its voter-ID law in recent years; older resources may still describe the former personal-identification-affidavit alternative. The current VoteIdaho guidance should control this record, and this section should be periodically reverified.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Idaho Election Day polling places and early-voting locations must meet federal accessibility requirements. Each voting location is required to provide accessible voting equipment with features that can include audio ballot transcription, enlarged text, adjustable contrast and adaptations for marking a ballot. Voters who need assistance may bring someone to help them vote or request assistance from an election worker. Any registered Idaho voter may also request an absentee ballot and vote without leaving home.
accessible_voting.internal_note: The official accessible-voting page directly establishes accessibility requirements for Election Day and early-voting locations, accessible equipment features, assistance options and absentee voting availability.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Idaho military and overseas voters covered by federal law have special registration and absentee-voting protections. Eligible voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as a backup if necessary. Military and overseas voters should use Idaho's official UOCAVA resources and their county elections office for current ballot-delivery and return instructions, because special deadlines and transmission options can apply.
military_overseas.internal_note: Idaho's official military and overseas voter resources implement federal UOCAVA procedures and provide access to FPCA and FWAB processes. This section deliberately avoids applying the ordinary domestic absentee deadline to UOCAVA voters because federal and state special procedures may provide different registration, transmission and return rules.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student may register and vote in Idaho if the student is an Idaho resident and otherwise meets the state's voter qualifications. The residence the student considers home, whether a college or university address or another Idaho address, is the address used for voting. An out-of-state student who has lived in Idaho for at least 30 days and establishes Idaho residence may register in Idaho using accepted identification and proof of residence. A student may be registered to vote in only one place. Idaho also accepts an enrollment letter from an Idaho high school or university as one form of proof of residence for in-person voter registration.
student_voting.internal_note: The official registration page contains a specific college-student section stating that students can register and vote while attending college in Idaho or maintain registration in their home state, that Idaho residence is required, that a student may be registered in only one place, and that an out-of-state student who has lived in Idaho for at least 30 days may register using accepted ID and proof of residence. The same page lists an enrollment letter from an Idaho high school or university as acceptable proof of residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Idaho voters can use VoteIdaho.gov to view a personalized sample ballot showing the contests and measures that apply to them. The 2026 General Election voter page provides the official sample-ballot tool so voters can preview what will appear on their ballot before voting.
sample_ballot.internal_note: The official 2026 General Election page currently provides a 'View Your Personalized Sample Ballot' function. VoteIdaho.gov's 12 Principles of Idaho Elections, [https://voteidaho.gov/12-principles-of-idaho-elections/](https://voteidaho.gov/12-principles-of-idaho-elections/), also identifies personalized sample ballots as an official voter-information service.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Idaho Secretary of State, Administration and Elections Office, Idaho State Capitol Building, East Wing, Second Floor, 700 W Jefferson, #E205, Boise, ID 83702. Phone: 208-334-2852. Office hours are Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Questions about individual registration records, local early-voting schedules, polling places and absentee ballots can also be directed to the voter's county elections office.
contact.internal_note: Current VoteIdaho.gov pages directly verify the Administration and Elections Office address, telephone number and Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. hours. The official pages expose the email address through protected rendering rather than reliably readable plain text in the retrieved source, so no email address is inserted into reader-facing content without direct verification. County election offices are linked throughout VoteIdaho.gov.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use VoteIdaho.gov, operated by the Idaho Secretary of State, for statewide voter registration, voter information lookup, election dates, voting requirements, absentee voting and personalized sample ballots. Idaho elections are administered locally by county clerks and county election offices, which provide local polling places, early-voting schedules and absentee-ballot services.
official_resources.internal_note: Official 2026 General Election resource: [https://voteidaho.gov/idaho-general-election/](https://voteidaho.gov/idaho-general-election/). Official voter registration: [https://voteidaho.gov/voter-registration/](https://voteidaho.gov/voter-registration/). Official 2026 election calendar: [https://voteidaho.gov/calendar/](https://voteidaho.gov/calendar/). Official accessibility guidance: [https://voteidaho.gov/accessible-voting/](https://voteidaho.gov/accessible-voting/). Official FAQ: [https://voteidaho.gov/frequently-asked-questions/](https://voteidaho.gov/frequently-asked-questions/). All source_url values and URLs embedded in internal notes are bare URL strings, and all reader-facing prose uses plain text rather than Markdown hyperlink syntax.
